summary: This PR adds measurement/harness tooling and archives the S-17 Bread calibration experiment without touching production engine, Auto recommendation, API, or database code. The reviewer's findings are limited to nits and minor issues: a missing error guard and unnecessary photo-loading in one comparison script, an unbounded/unchecked polling loop in a spike script, duplicated comparison logic across two scripts, an import-style inconsistency, and inconsistent HTML escaping in a local-only report generator. None of these findings indicate broken core logic, security exposure beyond negligible local-file risk, or missing documentation, and the PR's own validation (typecheck, 418 tests, lint, parity checks) passed. The change is low-risk, well-scoped tooling/archival work suitable to merge, with the identified minor issues worth addressing in follow-up polish rather than blocking.

findings.description: Imports use relative paths into ../../src/ rather than the repo's @/* alias convention (same in browser-stats.ts, desktop-stats.ts, harness.ts). If tsx resolves the tsconfig paths, the alias should be used; if not, a note is warranted so the relative paths aren't 'fixed' into breakage later.
findings.suggestion: Switch to @/lib/engines/... imports if tsx honors tsconfig paths, otherwise add a one-line comment in harness.ts explaining why relative paths are required.

findings.description: The STAT_FIELDS/PERCENTILES/bin-rounding comparison and the params-check block are duplicated nearly verbatim in desktop-stats.ts's compare(). The two scripts already share harness.ts; if the two parity definitions drift, the auditability these scripts exist to provide silently degrades.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared compareStats(offline, next) helper (alongside STAT_FIELDS and the tolerance constants) into harness.ts and use it from both scripts.

findings.description: Captions interpolate record['prediction_id'], entry['path'], and the size-mismatch note into HTML without html.escape, while figure() escapes src. All inputs are local maintainer-generated files so the blast radius is nil, but escaping is applied inconsistently within the same page.
findings.suggestion: html.escape the caption strings built in build_photo, or route all caption text through a helper that escapes.

findings.description: In compare(), `const a = base[id]` is used without a check while the download side is checked. With --baseline <older-file> (the reader explicitly supports the older bare { id: stats } shape) a missing id throws a TypeError instead of the documented clean exit 1. Additionally, the module-level photo-loading loop runs before argument handling, so even a pure --compare of two JSON files requires all licensed inputs to be present on disk.
findings.suggestion: Guard `if (!a)` with the same exit-1 message as the download side, and skip loading/hashing the photo inputs when --compare is given.

findings.description: The prediction polling loop has no timeout backstop and no poll.ok check: a prediction stuck in a non-terminal state, a non-2xx poll whose body parses to a prediction without a terminal status, or a fetch that keeps failing will spin forever. This matches the repo's explicit red flag about waits on external services without a timeout covering every non-terminal state.
findings.suggestion: Cap the loop (e.g. 10 minutes), check poll.ok, and exit non-zero naming the prediction id and its manual-cancel URL.

findings.description: A transient network error or HTTP error during polling throws an unhandled stack trace instead of the script's normal error reporting, and no record of any kind is written for a prediction that may still be billing. The finally block in main does clean up the upload, so the impact is a bad failure mode, not a leak.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the poll fetch, check poll.ok, and print a readable error (prediction id, status) before exiting non-zero.

implementation_correctness.justification: Core harness logic appears functional per PR's own validation (typecheck, tests, parity checks passing), but findings identify real correctness gaps: desktop-stats.ts's compare() lacks a guard for missing baseline entries (throws instead of clean exit) and unnecessarily loads all photo inputs even for pure JSON comparisons (F4); the spike script's polling loop has no timeout or ok-check, risking infinite hangs or unhandled crashes on transient errors (F5, F6). These are minor-severity and confined to auxiliary tooling/spike scripts, not production engine code.

idiomaticity.justification: Only a nit-level inconsistency was flagged: scripts use relative ../../src/ imports instead of the repo's @/* alias convention, with no indication this breaks anything, just a stylistic deviation worth a comment or fix (F1).

complexity.justification: The two comparison scripts duplicate the STAT_FIELDS/PERCENTILES/tolerance comparison logic nearly verbatim despite already sharing a harness module, creating a maintainability risk if the parity definitions drift apart (F2). This is a nit-level simplification opportunity rather than a structural complexity problem.

test_risk_coverage.justification: The PR reports a passing broader test suite (418 tests), but the findings surface risky, untested edge paths within the new scripts themselves: a missing-baseline-id case that throws ungracefully (F4), and an unbounded polling loop with no timeout or error handling for a long-running external call (F5, F6). These risky paths in new tooling code don't appear to be covered by targeted tests.

documentation.justification: No documentation-related findings were raised against the diff, and the PR body itself is thorough, explaining scope, validation performed, and what was deliberately left unfinished. No evidence of opaque or under-explained non-obvious decisions in the reviewed code.

security_safety.justification: One security-tagged nit was found: inconsistent HTML escaping in a local report-generation script (captions unescaped while image src is escaped), but the data source is local maintainer-generated content with no untrusted-input exposure, so blast radius is described as nil (F3).

verdictReason: All findings are nit or minor severity, confined to auxiliary experiment-measurement scripts and a spike script rather than production code, with no critical correctness, security, or regression issues; the PR explicitly changes no production engine/API/database behavior.
